title: Upgrade sentinel & regression sieve for LTS rollout gating
creator: Ava Patel
description: Build a purpose-built "sentinel and regression sieve" that augments current rollout checks with layered signals for LTS channel upgrades. Goal: detect subtle perf / quality regressions and enforce gated promotion into LTS and Dedicated clusters with automated rollback triggers and human-readable failure reasons.
acceptance_criteria: A reproducible end-to-end pipeline executes in <= 45 minutes for a standard release candidate against the regression sieve;
Signal set includes latency p50/p95/p99, token-cost delta, cache hit ratio, and an automated eval score delta for core prompt suite;
Gate decision is deterministic and expressed as pass/warn/fail with an artifact linking to failing traces and sample generations;
Canary cohort orchestration integrates with routing service to direct 1%/10% cohorts and automatically abort promotion on fail;
Playbook steps and owner assignments are surfaced in the Console runbook panel for each failed gate.
implementation_notes: We'll reuse the synthetic workload harness from ENG-62321 but add a lightweight QA evaluator that runs a curated 120-prompt set (diverse latencies and tasks) in parallel;
Use the runtime telemetry feature to emit a 'sieve.tag' per request so we can correlate KV cache behaviour with regressions without sampling loss;
Prefer non-blocking canary aborts that trigger controlled rollback via existing rollout-controller API;
To reduce flakiness, apply sliding-window smoothing for latency signals and require persistent deviation across two consecutive runs before failing;
Trade-off: higher sample counts reduce noise but increase runtime — target sweet spot measured in acceptance_criteria.
test_plan: Unit tests for signal aggregation logic and evaluation scorer (coverage > 85%);
Integration test that runs the sieve against a known-good RC and a purposely regressed RC to validate pass/fail paths;
Performance test to ensure the pipeline completes within the time budget on dedicated CI hardware;
Chaos test: simulate partial telemetry loss and validate gate behavior is conservative (favor warn over pass).
rollout_plan: Stage 1 (canary): wire the sieve to internal canary traffic (1%) for next three RCs;
Stage 2 (expanded): increase cohorts to 10% and enable automated 'warn' notifications to oncall;
Stage 3 (LTS gate): require two consecutive successful sieve runs as a hard rule before promoting to LTS channel;
Fallback: automatic model-variant fallback to a numerically compatible quantized build if regression is localized to a quantization kernel.
